subject: Follow-up: p95/p99 end-to-end latency & streaming/concurrency PoL plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Delphine Rousseau <delphine.rousseau@delphi-ai.com>, Samir Patel <samir@delphi-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: p95/p99 end-to-end latency & streaming/concurrency PoL plan

Hi Delphine / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared PoL (Proof-of-Load) plan for validating Redwood Hosted against your incumbent. I captured the items we discussed and added a few engineering details we’ll need to run a representative test.

Key acceptance goals (you confirmed approximate targets on the call):
- End-to-end p95 <= 350 ms (client observed, includes network)
- End-to-end p99 <= 1.2 s
- First-byte streaming latency for partial responses <= 150 ms for short prompts (<= 64 tokens)
- Sustained throughput target: 800–1,200 QPS for short-turn queries (50–150 tokens) with 8–16 concurrent connections per session

Proposed PoL scope and steps (attached: pol-load-plan.xlsx):
1) Traffic profile: run a 30m baseline ramp + 30m sustained window + 20m spike pattern (30–60% of baseline for 5m intervals). We’ll replay anonymized production traces you provide.
2) Concurrency model: simulate 1k concurrent (logical) users mapped to 12–16 backend concurrency slots — we want to validate prefix cache effectiveness and tail latency behavior.
3) Streaming validation: include a subset of streaming interactions (≈20% of traffic) to measure first-byte and chunk intervals.
4) Measurement: end-to-end measurements captured by your client-side probe + Redwood trace-id injection. We’ll provide an instrumentation header and a small SDK snippet.
5) Success criteria: test passes if p95/p99 and streaming FB numbers are within agreed targets for the sustained window AND no more than 3% of requests time out or degrade quality (fallbacks).

Logistics / asks from your side:
- A 1–2GB sample of anonymized traces (request sizes, token counts, client geos).
- A short list of 3–5 representative prompt templates for both short and long-turns.
- A test account/API key we can use for PoL calls (restricted, short-lived).
- Preferred window: Wed Jun 16 or Thu Jun 17 (your timezone).

Technical contacts: I’m looping in Marissa (solutions) and Ben (performance eng) to own execution & instrumentation.

Next steps: please confirm the targets above and the preferred PoL date. Once confirmed we’ll lock the runbook and share the lightweight SDK and the runbook steps.

Attachments: pol-load-plan.xlsx (PoL steps and traffic profiles)

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: p95/p99 end-to-end latency & streaming/concurrency PoL plan

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful and close to what we talked about. A few clarifications from our product/infra side: 

- Our incumbent numbers (end-to-end client observed) are roughly p95 ~ 420 ms, p99 ~ 1.8 s across our US clients today. We need a clear plan to get below those baselines before we can move forward.
- Streaming expectations: for short prompts we require first-byte <= 150 ms 90% of the time during steady-state; we also care about chunk spacing for longer streaming (>256 tokens).
- Concurrency: Samir reports typical sustained QPS of ~950 during peak windows with bursts to 1.6k QPS; concurrency per session varies but 10–14 concurrent backend calls is realistic.

We can supply: sample traffic traces (anonymized), three canonical prompt templates, and access to a staging key/account for the PoL. Wed Jun 16 works best for our infra team — mornings ET.

Couple of asks:
- Can Redwood simulate the same client geo diversity? We want to see US-east, US-west and EU West to understand cross-region variance.
- Please include a cold-start scenario (deploy fresh model instance) in the runbook so we know tail effects on the p99.

I’m attaching a short CSV with our observed p95/p99 buckets (see p95-p99-metrics.csv) for baseline comparison.

Best,
Delphine
Head of Product
Delphi AI

Delphine / Samir — thanks for the helpful notes and the CSV. Quick confirmation of our PoL approach and a proposed checklist so we can lock Wed Jun 16 morning ET.

What Redwood will deliver for the PoL:
- Multi-region simulation: yes — we will run synthetic clients from us-east, us-west and eu-west and report region-specific p95/p99 plus an aggregated client-observed metric.
- Cold-start injection: we will include two forced cold-start events during the sustained window (one at minute 10, one at minute 45). We’ll capture pre/post p99 deltas.
- Instrumentation: we will provide a small header (X-Redwood-Trace) to echo trace ids and return a JSON timing blob: {server_time_ms, kernel_ms, queue_ms}. We’ll also include a token-count header. (We’ll share the SDK snippet in the runbook.)
- Streaming knobs: chunk size and flush intervals are configurable in the test harness; we’ll expose 3 presets (aggressive, default, conservative) so you can see impact on first-byte and chunk spacing.

Acceptance criteria (formalized):
1) During the 30m sustained window: client-observed p95 <= 350 ms AND p99 <= 1.2 s for >= 90% of regions tested.
2) Streaming: first-byte latency <= 150 ms for >= 90% of short prompts under the sustained load.
3) Error floor: <3% requests with HTTP 5xx or timeouts.
4) Cold-start: p99 delta (cold vs warm) must not exceed 2x baseline for the majority of samples.

Request from your side for the run:
- Staging API key with 24h access (we’ll return logs after test).
- Sample prompt templates and the anonymized trace file you mentioned.
- A named point-of-contact (infra) on the day of the run for escalation.

We’ll draft the exact runbook and share it by EOD today; can you confirm a 09:30 ET start on Wed Jun 16?

Regards,
Ben Carter
Performance Engineering
Redwood Inference
